_how_to_edit: The story page, replay map and home hero read this file on every load. Edit it, run `node groundstop/src/build.js`, commit and push to main; no Squarespace edit is needed. Times are hours on an Eastern clock on Nov. 13, 2026 (17.5 = 5:30 p.m.; values past 24 mean Nov. 14). Set lift to null while the stop is in effect.
headline_status: The ground stop is still in effect
cause: Telecommunications outage at air traffic control
moments: A Friday afternoon, with flights departing on schedule across the country.
Flights bound for Chicago O’Hare are stopped over communications problems, and Midway follows three minutes later.
Nationwide ground stop. More than 3,100 flights already in the air are allowed to continue to their destinations.
The transportation secretary says a communication issue is affecting air route traffic control centers.
The FAA advisory now runs to 11:30 p.m. Eastern, and no end time is confirmed.
The FAA says a temporary telecommunications outage caused the stop, and officials say they see no sign of an attack.
facts: Eastern start time, the only one of the three stops to begin after noon
flights in the air when the stop began, allowed to finish their trips
flights delayed by about 5:20 p.m. Eastern, according to FlightAware; reported cancellations ranged from about 450 to more than 700
unknown: What is not known. The FAA blames a temporary telecommunications outage but has not said what caused the outage or when departures will resume. This replay ends at 5:20 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, the last time we checked, with the stop still in effect. Three days earlier, on Nov. 10, the agency expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. No official has connected the tool to the stop, and no reporting so far shows a link.
status_html: As of 5:20 p.m. Eastern on Friday the stop was still in effect, 1 hour and 26 minutes after it began. The FAA's advisory ran through 11:30 p.m., though the agency told airlines to hold departures until further notice, so that time is a planning window that can move in either direction. FlightAware had counted more than 9,000 delays for the day by then. Reports of its cancellation count between 5 and 5:20 p.m. ranged from about 450 to more than 700, so we are treating 450 as the floor.
compare_html: Friday's stop had already run 86 minutes by 5:20 p.m., nearly as long as the entire 2023 stop, and it began late on a Friday afternoon where the 2023 stop began early on a Wednesday. The more than 9,000 delays FlightAware counted by 5:20 p.m. were already close to the roughly 10,000 logged for the whole day in 2023, and Friday's count was still rising.
notknown_html:
The FAA has not said what caused the telecommunications outage. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a threat to the country and that the outage was separate from a global Microsoft outage one day earlier. CNN reported that two law enforcement officials said preliminary reports indicate it was not a cyberattack.

Three days before the stop, on Nov. 10, the FAA expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. No official has connected the tool to the stop, Mullin said he could not confirm whether the two are related, and no reporting so far shows a link.

This story reflects what was known at 5:20 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, 2026. We will update the end time, the cause and the final delay counts as the FAA and FlightAware report them.
